title: Health checks
description: Framework-neutral Fetch handlers for liveness (/healthz) and readiness (/readyz) with concurrent named checks, per-check timeouts, critical versus degraded results, redacted errors, and no-store JSON.

notes: Uses only standard Fetch Request/Response/Headers, AbortController, and timers; intended for Node.js 22+, Bun, Deno, Cloudflare Workers, Next.js route handlers, and Hono. Only Node.js 22 was exercised by repository tests.
No runtime packages, environment reads, or network access; the application supplies every check function and its dependencies.

configuration: checks: named functions (critical by default) or { check, critical?, timeoutMs? }. Each receives an AbortSignal that fires on timeout. Names match [A-Za-z0-9_.:-]{1,64}; at most 50 checks.
timeoutMs (default 2000, 1-60000), clock (epoch milliseconds, default Date.now), optional non-sensitive version label, livenessPath/readinessPath for handle().
exposeErrors (default false) adds truncated error messages; enable only behind a trusted internal network.
limitations: Every readiness request runs every check; there is no result caching, request coalescing, rate limiting, or authentication. Restrict exposure and probe frequency at the platform or proxy.
A timed-out check is reported and aborted via its signal, but a check that ignores the signal keeps running in the background.
detail strings returned by checks are included verbatim (control characters replaced, truncated to 256 characters); keep secrets and topology out of them.
No metrics export, startup probe semantics, dependency graph, or process-level self-healing is included.
Tests ran on Node.js 22 with in-process fake checks; no orchestrator or load balancer integration was exercised.
decisions: default paths /healthz (liveness) and /readyz (readiness); GET and HEAD only, others 405
a critical check fail or timeout → 503 fail; only non-critical failures → 200 degraded
per-check timeout default 2,000 ms; error messages hidden unless exposeErrors
